title: Paperboat protocol v0
description: Every message between the UI and a backend. Generated by hand from protocol/README.md; the source of truth for message shapes. protocol/golden.py and protocol/smoke_test.py validate every message a backend sends against it.

id.description: The component's label, in vector order.

type.description: signal (a value, the default), step (control in a Step flow), a value's shape (image, points, vector…), or any (any value but a step). A wire joins ports of one type; vector and legacy numbers are compatible.

unit.description: Its unit (N, m, rad, m/s…). A wire between two ports with units joins the same unit; a port without one takes any (#4).

dimension.description: A vector's fixed number of values. Absent: any length.

components.description: A vector's ordered component labels and optional per-component units; its length fixes the dimension.

unit.description: Its unit (kg, N/rad…), shown next to the field; a variable bound to it must be in the same unit.

ParamDef.description: A setting on a block, or a property of a station object. number and boolean reach the block as numbers (boolean: a checkbox, 1 or 0); text, key (a KeyboardEvent.code, picked by pressing it) and file (a path, relative to the descriptor) as text; enum (one of options, a dropdown) as its name (and to an expression, its index).

kind.description: source pushes into the domain, probe reads it, function computes, monitor shows a value on the Dashboard.

group.description: Palette group: the domain for its own blocks, else the toolkit package.

linked.description: Spawned by a station object (same id): not in the palette, no params, removed with it.

instrument.description: A monitor's instrument on the Dashboard: graph (default), display (the latest value) or image.

view.description: How the UI draws the block: a hint, so a UI without it (or a block without it) draws the normal card.

compact.description: Draw a small plate: a glyph, bare port dots (names on hover), the name and main value in a caption below.

glyph.description: The plate's glyph: a curve name (gain, plus, step, clamp, const) or a few characters drawn as text (&, ≥1, ¬).

value.description: The caption's value, an expression of the block's params: {k}, {min}…{max}.

forms.description: A magic block's forms; its inputs and outputs are the first's, and its form param (an enum) picks one.

ports_from.description: The id of a text param that decides the inputs: one per sign character in it (+ adds, - or − subtracts; at most 26; none reads as ++), ids a, b, c… of the first input's type. Sum's signs.

feedthrough.description: false: its outputs this step don't depend on its inputs this step (an integrator, a delay), so a feedback loop may pass through it. Absent: true.

description.description: One line in plain words: what it does. Shown on its card in the block browser. Optional.

links.description: Slots naming other station objects (a spring's a and b).

block.description: The linked block type it spawns on the Flow page, if any.

description.description: One line in plain words: what it does. Shown on its card in the block browser. Optional.

ObjectDef.description: A station object type: a thing on the Station page whose props are edited only there.

rot.description: Radians, applied in x, y, z order.

src.description: An image's picture: a URL or a data: URL.

Entity.description: One shape on the Station's scene. shape: box, sphere (size[0] = radius), line (pos to `to`), image (a size[0] x size[1] picture facing +z, from src).

View.description: Camera hint sent with a scene. 2d: orthographic, looking down -z at center, height units tall.

grid.description: Show the floor grid (default true). The user can switch it on or off on the Station page, and that choice wins.

camera.description: Where the camera opens, and where Home on the view cube returns it. Default: eye [2, 4, 8], looking at [0, 0, 0].

target.description: The point it looks at and orbits (default [0, 0, 0]).

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees (default 50).

links.description: Link slot to the id of the station object filling it.

pos.description: Where it sits in the Station's graph view.

ToolkitStatus.description: One optional external toolkit from toolkits.toml and its status on this machine.

required.description: Whether the current backend requires this toolkit.

versions.description: Available release versions from the remote repository, newest first.

default.description: Suggested default release version to install.

busy.description: Set while an operation is running for this toolkit.

toolkits.description: Available optional toolkits and their installed status on this machine.

variables.load.description: The backend's default variables, on connect after the scene, if it has any.

variables.values.description: What the variables come to (#36), so the UI shows formulas' values: on connect and after each variables.set. With error (and at, the variable or block at fault) when they don't hold.

values.description: Each variable's resolved value, by name.

v.description: The latest scalar or text sample, or a whole numeric vector on a Display monitor.

components.description: Labels and units for a vector Display sample, in vector order.

toolkits.status.description: Updated toolkit statuses sent while or after installing, updating, or uninstalling a toolkit.

variables.description: The variables the graph's and station's references use; absent: the last ones set.

variables.set.description: The user's variables changed: the backend checks them, keeps them for the next run, and answers with a scene (or a log error).

backend.restart.description: Ask the backend process to restart itself with the same command-line arguments.

toolkit.install.description: Install an optional toolkit from toolkits.toml and rebuild the engine.

version.description: Release tag (e.g. 0.1.0) or 'dev' for main branch. Absent: latest release or dev.

toolkit.versions.description: Fetch available release versions for an optional toolkit.

toolkit.update.description: Update an installed toolkit from its repository and rebuild the engine.

toolkit.uninstall.description: Remove an installed optional toolkit and rebuild the engine.

pos.description: Its place on the Flow canvas; backends ignore it.

DashboardLayout.description: The Dashboard's grid: where each monitor block's instrument sits and how big it is, plus decorations (sections, separators, labels) and tabs. A backend ships one as its default (the descriptor's [dashboard]); an instrument not listed falls in where the automatic order puts it, and a block that does not exist is ignored. Decorations and tabs belong to the layout, not the flow: the Flow canvas still decides which instruments exist.

columns.description: Grid columns; the UI fits fewer on a narrow screen.

size.description: compact: a readout card (1x1 cells); normal: a plot or picture to read at a glance (2x1); large: one to study (2x2); xlarge: one to fill the page with (3x3). Absent: the kind's default (display compact, graph normal, image large).

tab.description: The tab it is on (one of `tabs`); absent: the first.

tabs.description: Pages of the Dashboard, each with its own grid. A tab strip shows when there are two or more. Absent: one page.

decorations.description: Things that are not instruments. section: a titled frame round a group of cells (takes no cells; `at` and `span` [w, h]). hline / vline: a separator on a grid line, in the gap, along `span` columns (hline, from the top of `at`'s row) or rows (vline, down the left of `at`'s column); takes no cells. label: text that takes cells like an instrument (`span` [w, h], default [2, 1]); a section's title and a label's text may hold `{block}` or `{block:.2f}`, which show that monitor's latest value (`{{` and `}}` are braces). console: the Console's lines, in a frame that takes cells (`span` [w, h], default [4, 3]); it has no text. station: a read-only view of the Station (the 3D scene), in a frame that takes cells (`span` [w, h], default [4, 3]); it has no text and no editing.

text.description: A section's title, or a label's text. `{name}` shows the monitor block's latest value (else the variable's value), `{block:.2f}` with that many decimals; `{{` and `}}` are literal braces.

span.description: A separator's length in cells (a whole number); a section's, label's or console's size [columns, rows].

style.description: A label's look: heading (default) or note.

tab.description: The tab it is on (one of `tabs`); absent: the first.

GraphGroup.description: A group of blocks. subsystem: a block you open to see its insides, like a Simulink subsystem; its ports are the wires crossing its edge. story: a subsystem that runs as one step of a Step flow (ports in -> next): its blocks once per clock step for params.seconds (0: once), fresh each time if params.reset. visual: a frame that tidies the canvas only. Groups nest (parent); the graph's wires stay flat, block to block, so backends treat a subsystem or a frame as if it weren't there.

nodes.description: Its blocks (not the groups in it: those name it as their parent).

parent.description: The group it is in (a subsystem, story or frame); absent: the top level.

pos.description: Its top-left on the whole canvas; backends ignore it.

seconds.description: How long the story runs when a path arrives (0: once).

reset.description: Its blocks start afresh each time a path arrives (a story in a loop starts over).

ports.description: Where a subsystem's or story's ports sit on its block (ids are node::port, or in and next). Backends ignore it.

items.description: [node, port] output to clear when a story leaves.

release.description: Story outputs that read as unwired after its path leaves.

ParamValue.description: A param's value: a number, true / false (a boolean param), or text (text, key and file params). Or a reference (#36): {"var": name} takes a variable's value; {"expr": formula} (number and boolean params) a formula over variables. The backend resolves references before it makes blocks and objects.

expr.description: A formula over number and boolean variables: + - * / ^ %, comparisons, && || ?:, sqrt, sin, min, clamp…

NodeState.description: What a run says about a block. A Step flow sends running (a path arrived) and done (it left); any run sends failed for the block at fault.

StationView.description: How the Station page shows the station: the built-in scene, a graph of station objects, or the backend's own page (web; page is its path on the backend's port).

EntityPatch.description: A changed entity in scene.patch: its id and what changed.

rot.description: Radians, applied in x, y, z order.

src.description: An image's picture: a URL or a data: URL.

Form.description: One form of a magic block: the ports it has in that form (signal: computes; step: branches on a Step flow's path). The block's form param picks one.

RunSettings.description: How a run goes. The backend's defaults come in hello.run; graph.run may override any of them except mode.

mode.description: clock: every step for duration (and every Step flow); once: a Signal flow evaluated a single time.

duration.description: Run length, s (a Step flow: its limit).

speed.description: Times real time (1: as the clock goes; 0: as fast as it can).

node.progress.description: How far a block's long step has got (Context::progress), at most ~20 a second per block.

Variable.description: A named, typed value (#36), used by reference in block params and station props. Exactly one of value and expr.

name.description: Letters, digits and _; not t, pi, e or a function's name.

value.description: Of its type: a number, true / false, or text (enum: one of options).

expr.description: A number or boolean variable's formula over other variables, instead of a value.

step.description: How much one nudge in the UI changes it.

exposed.description: Also a control on the Dashboard, for operators.

Variables.description: The variables of a backend (its defaults) or the user's.

PortSides.description: Where a block's ports sit on the Flow canvas: the port ids on each side, in order. A port not listed keeps its place (inputs on the left, outputs on the right, after the listed ones). Backends ignore it.

Project.description: A project file (#82): everything a user made, as one JSON file (name.paperboat.json). It is not a protocol message; the UI writes and reads it. flow, station, variables and dashboard are the shapes the protocol already uses. A block whose type the opening backend lacks stays as a lost block, params and wires kept.

paperboat.description: The project format version. Opening refuses a newer one and says so.

backend.description: The engine the project was made on (hello.engine). Opening it on another backend warns first.

flow.description: The Flow canvas, groups included; every node has its place (pos).

variables.description: The user's variables: the list the Variables sheet shows.

dashboard.description: The user's Dashboard arrangement, if they made one.

run.description: Only the run settings the user changed from the backend's defaults.
